title: A universal tensor-kernel witness gives eventual transition factorizations
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $I$ a small nonempty directed partially ordered set, and $(M_s,f_{st})_{s\in I}$ a directed system of finitely presented $R$-modules [def-sc-finitely-presented-module]. Let $u_s:M_s\to M$ be compatible maps exhibiting an $R$-module $M$ as the colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Fix $i\in I$, an $R$-module $T$, and $z\in M_i\otimes_RT$ with $(u_i\otimes\mathrm{id}_T)(z)=0$. Assume that for every finitely presented $R$-module $Q$ and every $x\in\ker(u_i\otimes\mathrm{id}_Q)$ there exists an $R$-linear map $q:T\to Q$ such that $(\mathrm{id}_{M_i}\otimes q)(z)=x$. Tensor products and induced maps are [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Then there is $j\ge i$ such that for every $k\ge j$ there exists an $R$-linear map $h_k:M_k\to M_j$ with $f_{ij}=h_k\circ f_{ik}$. No Mittag-Leffler or flatness hypothesis is imposed on $M$ or $T$, and $I$ need not be countable.

source.place: Tag 059M (proposition-ML-tensor), proof of (2) implies (1), death of the product-kernel element, implemented directly in the given colimit as in Tag 059L (lemma-kernel-tensored-fp); Tag 059E (proposition-ML-characterization), proof of (2) implies (3), using Tag 059D (lemma-domination) and Tag 059C (lemma-domination-fp).

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-commutes-with-colimits], the modules $M_s\otimes_RT$, with transition maps $f_{st}\otimes\mathrm{id}_T$ and legs $u_s\otimes\mathrm{id}_T$, have colimit $M\otimes_RT$. The indexing category is small and filtered because $I$ is a small nonempty directed poset. Apply the zero criterion of [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-modules-elementwise] to the given $z$: there is $j\ge i$ with $(f_{ij}\otimes\mathrm{id}_T)(z)=0$. Fix this $j$ for the rest of the proof.

source.place: Tags 059L (lemma-kernel-tensored-fp), its proof applied directly in the prescribed system, and 059M (proposition-ML-tensor), death of the universal kernel element; tensor-colimit input Tag 00DD and zero criterion Tag 00D7.

proof.text: For every finitely presented $Q$ and $x\in\ker(u_i\otimes\mathrm{id}_Q)$ choose the map $q:T\to Q$ in the hypothesis. The bilinear universal property [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] gives $(f_{ij}\otimes\mathrm{id}_Q)(\mathrm{id}_{M_i}\otimes q)=(\mathrm{id}_{M_j}\otimes q)(f_{ij}\otimes\mathrm{id}_T)$: both send $m\otimes t$ to $f_{ij}(m)\otimes q(t)$, and pure tensors generate. Consequently $(f_{ij}\otimes\mathrm{id}_Q)(x)=0$. If $k\ge j$, compatibility $u_i=u_k f_{ik}$ implies $\ker(f_{ik}\otimes\mathrm{id}_Q)\subseteq\ker(u_i\otimes\mathrm{id}_Q)\subseteq\ker(f_{ij}\otimes\mathrm{id}_Q)$. The first inclusion follows by composing the tensor maps; it needs no flatness.

source.place: Tag 059M (proposition-ML-tensor), second tensor-product square in (2) implies (1); Tag 059E (proposition-ML-characterization), (2) implies (3), transitivity of the kernel inclusions.

proof.text: Fix $k\ge j$. By [def-sc-finitely-presented-module] choose a finite presentation $R^a\xrightarrow{A}R^b\xrightarrow{p}M_k\to0$ and finite generators $v_1,\ldots,v_c$ of $M_i$ from its finite presentation. Choose $w_r\in R^b$ with $p(w_r)=f_{ik}(v_r)$. Then $C=M_k/f_{ik}(M_i)$ has presentation $R^{a+c}\xrightarrow{(A,w_1,\ldots,w_c)}R^b\to C\to0$. Indeed the last map is surjective, and a vector $y$ maps to zero precisely when $p(y)=\sum_r\lambda_r f_{ik}(v_r)$ for some $\lambda_r\in R$; this is equivalent to $y-\sum_r\lambda_rw_r\in\ker p=\operatorname{im}A$. This identifies its kernel with the image of the displayed finite matrix, so $C$ is finitely presented.

source.place: Tag 059E (proposition-ML-characterization), (2) implies (3), finite presentation of the transition cokernel; the finite-matrix argument spells out this elementary assertion.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-tensor-kernel-factorization] with $U=M_i$, $V=M_k$, $W=M_j$, $f=f_{ik}$ and $g=f_{ij}$. Step 3 supplies its finitely presented cokernel hypothesis, and step 2 supplies its kernel inclusion for every finitely presented test module $Q$. Obtain $h_k:M_k\to M_j$ with $f_{ij}=h_k\circ f_{ik}$. This works for every $k\ge j$ with the same $j$ chosen in step 1, proving the conclusion.

lean.statement: theorem exists_eventual_factorization_of_tensor_witness (R : Type u) [CommRing R] {I : Type v} [PartialOrder I] [Nonempty I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)] (F : I ⥤ ModuleCat.{max u v w} R) [∀ s : I, Module.FinitePresentation R (F.obj s)] (c : Cocone F) (hc : IsColimit c) (i : I) (T : Type t) [AddCommGroup T] [Module R T] (z : F.obj i ⊗[R] T) (hz : (c.ι.app i).hom.rTensor T z = 0) (hwitness : ∀ (Q : Type (max u v w)) [AddCommGroup Q] [Module R Q] [Module.FinitePresentation R Q], ∀ x : F.obj i ⊗[R] Q, (c.ι.app i).hom.rTensor Q x = 0 → ∃ q : T →ₗ[R] Q, q.lTensor (F.obj i) z = x) : ∃ (j : I) (hij : i ≤ j), ∀ (k : I) (hjk : j ≤ k), ∃ h : F.obj k →ₗ[R] F.obj j, (F.map (homOfLE hij)).hom = h.comp (F.map (homOfLE (hij.trans hjk))).hom
